name: Street Custom 'Scorpion Tail' Chain Whip
description: A weapon constructed from salvaged motorcycle chain weighted at the tip with a sharpened steel slug, often augmented with welded barbs or razor wire wrapping. The Scorpion Tail has a 1.5-meter reach and can be swung with enough force to crack bone through light armor, while the weighted tip and barbs tear flesh on contact. It folds compact for concealment along a belt or inside a coat sleeve and deploys instantly with a flick of the wrist. The weapon has deep roots in Tier 1 street culture where it serves as both a personal defense weapon and a status symbol — the condition, decoration, and customization of a fighter's chain tells their history.
specifications: chain length: 1.5 meters tip weight: 200-400g sharpened steel slug barb configuration: Variable — razor wire, welded spikes, or hooked links folded length: 20 cm coiled weight: 0.8-1.5 kg depending on chain gauge material: Salvaged motorcycle or industrial chain
story_hooks: A fighting tournament in Tier 1 exclusively uses Scorpion Tails and has become a major gambling draw — the prize pool has attracted corporate attention and the fighters are being scouted as assets.
A specific chain whip style with distinctive link markings has appeared across three unrelated crime scenes — the markings indicate a single forge source that someone wants found.

physical_description.visual_profile: A coiled length of heavy-gauge motorcycle chain terminating in a brutal weighted steel head. When deployed, it presents as a predatory whip—controlled chaos with malevolent intent. The tip slug is visibly sharpened to a dull point, often wrapped or studded with razor wire that catches light. The overall impression is street-level lethality: crude, effective, and unmistakably dangerous.
physical_description.dimensions: Deployed length: 150 cm. Folded coil: 20 cm diameter × 8 cm height. Tip slug: 4 cm length × 2.5 cm diameter. Chain link pitch: 1.2 cm standard.
physical_description.weight_description: Heavy and unforgiving—0.8 to 1.5 kg depending on chain gauge and barb load. Feels substantial in the hand when coiled, with the tip weight creating a pronounced center-of-mass bias. Swing momentum builds quickly; demands respect and training to control.
physical_description.primary_material: Salvaged motorcycle or industrial-grade steel chain (Grade 80 or higher). Weighted tip is hardened steel, often scavenged from bearing housings or suspension components. Barbing uses razor wire, welded spikes, or hooked chain links.
physical_description.finish: Heavily oxidized steel with patchy rust bloom in places—some links show chrome plating worn to bare metal. The tip slug is either bare steel (gunmetal gray, slightly pitted) or crude case-hardened black. Razor wire wrapping shows copper oxidation at edges.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray and rust-red oxide, with black heat-treated accents on the tip. Razor wire catches as dull silver. Some units feature acid-etched owner marks or gang colors spray-painted onto select links.
physical_description.grip_texture: The chain handle end is typically wrapped with electrical tape, paracord, or leather scraps—tactile and non-slip even when wet. The wrapping is often filthy, stained with sweat and hydraulic fluid from years of carry.
distinctive_features: Weighted steel slug tip with visible sharpening marks and grinding striations
Razor wire or barbed-hook wrapping cascading down the final 15-20 cm of chain
Oxidation patterns and discoloration indicating field use and maintenance neglect
Custom etchings, gang tags, or owner initials gouged into the tip or chain links
Uneven chain links where sections have been welded, cut, or reinforced by previous owners
Corrosion bloom around welded spikes or hooked modifications
Tattered grip wrapping showing multiple repair layers underneath
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: No corporate branding—Street Custom is a loose collective of street armorers. Some pieces carry crude stamped initials (the maker's mark) on the tip slug. Chain may retain faint original manufacturer stamps from its salvage source (ANSI, ISO, or motorcycle brand logos), now mostly worn away.
physical_description.condition_typical: Battle-worn and field-patched. Surface shows active corrosion in humid GLMZ climate. Grip wrapping is stained and fraying. Barbs and spikes may show impact deformation or missing teeth from hard use. Owner customization is visible—dings, scratches, and deliberate marks that map the weapon's combat history.
